paragraphs.title: Prayer to God and the Psalm's Opening

easy.explanation: The psalm begins, "Hear me when I call, O God of my righteousness."
easy.q: To whom does the speaker call in prayer?

answers: It is intended for musical performance
It is intended as a battle speech
easy.explanation: The words "To the chief Musician on Neginoth" indicate a musical setting.
easy.q: What does the opening instruction indicate about the psalm?

easy.explanation: The speaker asks, "have mercy upon me, and hear my prayer."
easy.q: What does the speaker ask God to hear?

answers: That God enlarged him in distress
medium.explanation: He recalls, "thou hast enlarged me when I was in distress."
medium.q: What does the speaker remind God of when asking Him to answer?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to a period of trouble or hardship.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does "in distress" describe?

answers: He asks God to answer, recalls God's help, and asks God to hear his prayer
He rebukes his enemies, offers sacrifices, and goes to sleep
He asks for riches, victory, and musical instruments
medium.explanation: The prayer includes a request for an answer, a remembrance of past help, and a plea for God to hear.
medium.q: Which sequence best describes the speaker's prayer?

answers: It is a speech to human opponents
It is a description of sleep
challenge.explanation: The speaker directly addresses God and asks Him to hear a personal prayer.
challenge.q: What does the direct address "O God of my righteousness" reveal about the nature of the passage?

answers: God's past help gives him reason to ask for help again
Past distress proves that prayer is useless
The distress was caused by musical instruments
challenge.explanation: Because God enlarged him in distress before, the speaker confidently asks God to answer him now.
challenge.q: What connection does the speaker make between past distress and his present request?

answers: It is addressed to the chief Musician and associated with stringed instruments
It mentions the light of God's countenance
challenge.explanation: The opening direction, "To the chief Musician on Neginoth," identifies a musical setting.
challenge.q: Which detail identifies the psalm's intended setting?

paragraphs.title: Rebuke of the Opponents and a Call to Trust God

easy.explanation: He asks, "how long will ye turn my glory into shame?"
easy.q: What does the speaker say his opponents turn into shame?

answers: He sets him apart for Himself
He sends him to his enemies
easy.explanation: The psalm says, "the LORD hath set apart him that is godly for himself."
easy.q: What does the LORD do for the one who is godly?

easy.explanation: The command is, "put your trust in the LORD."
easy.q: In whom does the speaker tell the people to put their trust?

medium.explanation: Here, "leasing" means lying, falsehood, or deceit.
medium.q: What does the KJV phrase "seek after leasing" mean in context?

answers: Sin not, commune with their hearts, and be still
medium.explanation: The instruction is, "Stand in awe, and sin not," followed by inward reflection and stillness.
medium.q: What are the opponents told to do after being told to stand in awe?

medium.explanation: The verse says, "Offer the sacrifices of righteousness, and put your trust in the LORD."
medium.q: What action is joined with the command to trust the LORD?

answers: God's willingness to hear provides a reason to trust Him
God's hearing leads people to seek falsehood
challenge.explanation: The speaker presents the LORD as one who hears when called, giving a basis for confidence in Him.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the LORD hearing the speaker and the command to trust Him?

answers: A change from shameful falsehood to reflection, righteous worship, and trust in God
A change from prayer to sleep and material pleasure
A change from righteous worship to dishonoring others
challenge.explanation: The section moves the opponents away from vanity and falsehood toward stillness, righteousness, and trust.
challenge.q: What change in conduct is urged throughout this section?

challenge.explanation: The language of the heart, the bed, and stillness suggests private reflection and self-examination.
challenge.q: What does the instruction to commune with one's heart upon one's bed and be still suggest?

paragraphs.title: God's Light, Inner Joy, and Security

easy.explanation: He prays, "LORD, lift thou up the light of thy countenance upon us."
easy.q: What does the speaker ask the LORD to lift upon the people?

easy.explanation: The speaker says, "Thou hast put gladness in my heart."
easy.q: Where has the LORD put gladness?

easy.explanation: He can sleep because the LORD makes him dwell in safety.
easy.q: What enables the speaker to lie down and sleep in peace?

answers: It is an inward joy rather than a joy dependent on crops and wine
It comes only from corn and wine
It depends on defeating his enemies
medium.explanation: The speaker's gladness is in his heart, while others rejoice when their corn and wine increase.
medium.q: How is the speaker's gladness different from the joy connected with others' material abundance?

answers: A request for God's light, gladness in the heart, and peaceful security
medium.explanation: The passage moves from God's countenance to inner gladness and finally to peaceful sleep.
medium.q: What is the order of ideas in this section?

medium.explanation: To dwell in safety means to live securely and under protection.
medium.q: What does the word "safety" mean in the final verse?

answers: God's favorable presence is presented as the source of inner joy
Gladness comes only from material abundance
challenge.explanation: The request for God's light is followed by the testimony of gladness in the heart, linking God's presence with inner joy.
challenge.q: What connection is suggested between the light of God's countenance and gladness in the heart?

answers: The speaker depends on the LORD alone for security
The speaker has no protection at all
The speaker depends on other people's abundance
challenge.explanation: The word "only" emphasizes that the LORD alone is the source of the speaker's safety.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the word "only" in "thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety"?

answers: Many seek outward good, while the speaker finds joy and security in God
challenge.explanation: The many ask who will show them good, but the speaker points to God's light, inner gladness, and protection.
challenge.q: What major contrast appears in this section?
